prompt: Assess visible tyre condition, not physical depth or legal safety. First examine what is actually visible: groove relief and rubber between grooves, wear across the tread face, surface cracking, exposed cords or torn rubber. Distinguish tread DESIGN from CONDITION: the existence of longitudinal lines, zigzags or lugs alone does not prove good condition. Look for raised tread edges and recessed grooves versus broad smooth flattened rubber, faint shallow remnants or locally bald/worn areas. Do not demand a millimetre measurement or a visible TWI to judge visual wear. Mud, shadows and highlights can hide grooves or mimic cracks; do not invent concealed detail or equate dirt with damage. Then classify: bad if clear flattened/bald/shallow-looking wear or visible cracking, cords, tears or severe damage is present. Clear bad evidence is sufficient even when only part of the tyre is visible. good if enough tread face shows distinct groove/raised relief without clear wear or damage; this is only a visual screen. review if only sidewall/rim is shown without clear damage, tread detail is obscured, or wear evidence genuinely conflicts. A partial but clear tread face can suffice; do not automatically reject oblique views. No measured depth, TWI verification, hidden condition or roadworthiness claims. Judge this image alone. Return only a JSON object with exactly one key visual_condition and value good, bad, or review.
